items.q: What did the hacker find on Bartlett in 20 minutes?
items.a: An old email, a gym from 12 years ago and **old passwords from data breaches**.

items.q: How big was the National Public Data breach?
items.a: About **2.8 billion records**, so most adults over 30 likely have a full address history and ID numbers out there.

items.q: What worries him about cheap connected devices?
items.a: Almost all he examined **communicate with China**, which concerns him more than phone eavesdropping.

items.q: What does a credit freeze do?
items.a: It only **stops new cards, loans or mortgages** being opened in your name, and costs nothing.

items.q: Which account protection does he rely on?
items.a: **Hardware security keys** (YubiKey) wherever supported, plus Apple Advanced Data Protection and lockdown mode.
A **VPN** and **antivirus even on a Mac**, since Mac just has a different attack surface.

items.q: Can you erase your leaked data?
items.a: You can **opt out of data brokers**, but you cannot remove breached data from a hacker’s drive.
Third-party installs can bring **remote access Trojans**; he calls the iPhone safer.
A **nihilistic online extortion group and offshoots** that groom bullied, isolated children on every platform.

items.q: Why does he refuse to name the groups?
items.a: **Notoriety is what they want**, so naming them feeds the harm.

items.q: How big is the FBI response?
items.a: Public reports cite **500+ targets** and **58 field offices** mobilised.
